title: Block Tree Optimization: Flattening Dynamic Nodes via openBlock & dynamicChildren

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Imagine a 10-story skyscraper where only two lightbulbs in the entire building are dynamic. In older frameworks, an inspector has to walk into every single room on all 10 floors to check for burnt-out bulbs. Vue 3's Block Tree collects those two lightbulbs into a tiny express elevator list (`dynamicChildren`). When an update happens, the inspector skips all 10 floors and checks only those two specific bulbs in one step.
progressiveExplaining.junior: The Block Tree is Vue 3's compiler technique to flatten the Virtual DOM. When compiling a template, Vue creates a **Block** root (`openBlock()`). Any nested element with dynamic bindings inside that block is tracked in a flat array called `dynamicChildren`. When updating, Vue **skips traversing static DOM elements completely** and iterates over the flat `dynamicChildren` array directly, reducing diffing work from `O(total nodes)` to `O(dynamic nodes)`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Block Tree optimization decouples Virtual DOM update performance from total template size. Static subtrees (e.g. static SVGs, marketing paragraphs) are completely invisible to the update pass. Structural directives (`v-if`, `v-for`) break the flat array into nested Block boundaries (a tree of blocks), ensuring that conditional branches and list items maintain their own localized `dynamicChildren` arrays without corrupting parent flat indexes.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In the compiled code, a template begins with `(_openBlock(), _createElementBlock('div', null, [...]))`. `_openBlock()` initializes a global `currentBlock` array. Whenever `_createVNode()` runs with a `patchFlag > 0`, it pushes that dynamic VNode directly onto `currentBlock`. `_createElementBlock()` captures this array onto `vnode.dynamicChildren`. During `patchElement()`, if `vnode.dynamicChildren` exists, Vue executes `patchBlockChildren()`, looping strictly over `dynamicChildren` and ignoring static child nodes.

codeComparison.title: Deep Tree Traversal vs Block Tree Flat Array Iteration
codeComparison.summary: Traditional VDOM traverses 100 nested static nodes to find 1 dynamic text binding; Block Trees diff only the 1 dynamic node.

legacyOrBad.label: Full Recursive Tree Traversal (Vue 2)
legacyOrBad.snippet: patchChildren(n1, n2); // ❌ Traverses 100 static divs to find 1 dynamic child

modernOrGood.label: Vue 3 Block Tree (Flat Array Diff)
modernOrGood.snippet: for (let i = 0; i < dynamicChildren.length; i++) patch(dynamicChildren[i]); // ✅ O(dynamic)

interviewGotchas.question: Why do structural directives like `v-if` and `v-for` act as Block boundaries inside the Block Tree?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your deep understanding of why flat arrays cannot safely span dynamic conditionals.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: If a `v-if` conditional branch could be flattened into the parent block's `dynamicChildren` array, toggling the condition would change the length and order of the flat array, corrupting the index-based diffing of subsequent dynamic children. Therefore, `v-if` and `v-for` create **nested Block boundaries** (`openBlock()`), maintaining localized flat dynamic children arrays that can be cleanly swapped or keyed.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: A template is not a single flat list; it is a **Tree of Blocks** where blocks are separated by `v-if`, `v-else`, and `v-for` boundaries.

interviewGotchas.question: What is 'Static Hoisting' and how does it work alongside the Block Tree?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of compiler static node optimization.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: **Static Hoisting** extracts completely static subtrees (nodes with zero dynamic bindings) outside the render function so they are instantiated as VNode objects *once* at module evaluation time. On subsequent re-renders, the exact same VNode reference is reused, completely bypassing VNode creation and memory allocation.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Hoisted static VNodes are never included in `dynamicChildren` arrays.
